# <span id="aanchor476"></span> Master Allocation Setup

[&lt;&lt; Back](Master%20Allocation%20-%20Setup.md) \| [Gas Allocation](Master%20Allocation%20-%20Setup%20-%20Gas.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Liquid Allocation</a>

## Liquid Allocation

The allocation process for liquid meters ensures that, for each day, values are available for GSV, NSV, mass, components, and net allowable, and that availability is consistent between each master and member meter. For the allocation process to occur, all meters within the allocation must have the same data values for the time frame selected; otherwise, an exception will be generated.

<div class="procedure">

To set up a master location (liquid):

1.  Go to **Tools** \> **Master Allocation** \> **Setup**.

2.  Click the **Liquid** radio button.

3.  Click **New**.

4.  Select a liquid location to become the master location.

    The master location can only contain meter members, and must have a base direction of either inlet or outlet. Locations with a different direction will not be available in the drop-down list.

5.  Select the date range for the allocation.

6.  Use the Available Meters list to locate meters to include in the allocation. Double-click a meter to move it to the Meter Members list, or select multiple meters and click the right arrow button.

7.  Indicate the meters that you want to <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">keep whole<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>Volume, energy, and mass for meters that are "kept whole" in the allocation process will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit.</span></a> during the allocation process.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 558;height: 440;" />

If a direction has not been defined for a meter in Meter Characteristics, you will be prompted to select a direction. Meters without an assigned direction will be highlighted with a red and white border.

</div>

#### Liquid Calculation Method

When calculating allocation values for a master location, the balance arithmetic used is based on the base direction of the master.

For master locations with an inlet base direction:

<span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Location</span>= <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters</span>

For master locations with an outlet base direction:

<span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Location</span> = <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters</span>

Direction refers to the direction of the master location as defined in the Location Editor.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example 1">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example 1 - Liquid Allocation</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example 1">

A master location has three meter members (Meter 1 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\], Meter 2 \[<span style="color: #ff0000;">inlet</span>\], and Meter 3 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\]).

The master location has direction set to outlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used:

<span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Location </span>= <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters</span>



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 417;height: 338;" />

For Volume:

The master total volume differs from the member total volume.

Difference = Master Total Volume – Member Total Volume

560 - 575 = -15

This difference must be allocated proportionally across member meters.

Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total)

> | Meter |            Allocation            |
> |:-----:|:--------------------------------:|
> |   1   | -15 \* (360 / 575) = **- 9.39**  |
> |   2   |  -15 \* (-195 / 575) = **5.09**  |
> |   3   | -15 \* (410 / 575) = **- 10.70** |

The allocation will then be added to each member’s volume to create a revised allocated volume per meter.

> | Meter | Original Volume | Allocation | Revised Volume |
> |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:|
> |   1   |       360       |   -9.39    |     350.61     |
> |   2   |      -195       |    5.09    |     189.91     |
> |   3   |       410       |   -10.70   |     399.30     |
> | Total |       575       |    N/A     |      560       |

The revised member total volume now equals the master total volume.

Energy and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example 2">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example 2 - Liquid Allocation with Keep Whole</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example 2">

A master location has three meter members (Meter 1 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\], Meter 2 \[<span style="color: #ff0000;">inlet</span>\], and Meter 3 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\]).

The master location has direction set to inlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used:

<span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Location</span>= <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters</span>



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 417;height: 338;" />

Meter 3 will be "kept whole", indicating that the volume, energy, and mass for that meter will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit.

For Energy:

The energy of the kept whole meter will be subtracted from the master total to create a new master total for allocation.

New Master Total Energy = Master Total Energy - Kept Whole Energy

765 - 115 = 650

The energy for the kept whole meter will not be included in the member meter total. Without Meter 3, the meter member total energy is 780.

1380 - 600 = 780

The new master total energy differs from the new member total energy.

Difference = New Master Total Energy – New Member Total Energy

650 - 780 = -130

This difference must be allocated proportionally across the two member meters that are not being kept whole.

Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total)

> | Meter |            Allocation            |
> |:-----:|:--------------------------------:|
> |   1   |  -130 \* (-600 / 780) = **100**  |
> |   2   | -130 \* (1380 / 780) = **- 230** |
> |   3   |         N/A (kept whole)         |

The allocation will then be added to each member’s energy to create a revised allocated energy per meter.

> | Meter | Original Energy | Allocation | Revised Energy |
> |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:|
> |   1   |      -600       |    100     |      -500      |
> |   2   |      1380       |    -230    |      1150      |
> |   3   |       115       |     0      |      115       |
> | Total |       895       |    N/A     |      765       |

The revised member total energy now equals the master total.

Volume and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

</div>
